1.explanation:
All of these files participate in producing a working container‐style tab.  

• packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.config.js  
  This file defines the Sass tokens and mixins for the tabs.  We need to update it to emit the overflow:hidden, white-space:nowrap and text-overflow:ellipsis rules under the “.bx--tabs--container” modifier so that container tabs can be truncated.  

• packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.js  
  This is the vanilla (non-React) implementation of the container tabs.  Although most of the styling comes from the generated CSS, any className adjustments or default settings for the container variant live here; you may need to ensure the correct modifier class is applied and that there is no JavaScript logic preventing the CSS truncation.  

• packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js  
  This is where the <Tabs type="container" /> prop is turned into the “bx--tabs--container” class on the wrapper.  Confirm that the modifier class is present on that element so the Sass rules will match.  

• packages/react/src/components/Tab/Tab.js  
  This renders the <a> inside each <Tab>, including the title attribute for tooltips.  Verify that it is not overriding or resetting any overflow styles (for example, by wrapping the label in an extra element without overflow hidden) and that the generated CSS selector (“.bx--tabs--container .bx--tabs__nav-link”) will reach the correct DOM node.  

Together, these four files control both the application of the container modifier and the CSS rules that enforce truncation; updates to each may be required to restore the 16px-from-edge ellipsis behavior found in the default tab style.
1.bug_scenario: When the Tabs component is rendered with type="container" the labels are allowed to grow indefinitely instead of being truncated at the right‐hand edge.  In the default (non-container) style the tab text is automatically limited (overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis) so long labels get cut off cleanly and show a tooltip.  In the container style that truncation never kicks in, so long titles push the following tabs aside or wrap, and no ellipsis appears.

2.explanation:
• packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js
  – This is the React component that applies the `--container` modifier class (`bx--tabs--container`) on the root `<div>`. Any CSS fixes for truncation under the container variant will target that class or need to be surfaced here if we need to pass extra props to the Tab children.

• packages/react/src/components/Tab/Tab.js
  – This renders the individual `<a>` element (`bx--tabs__nav-link`) with the label inside. It currently doesn’t add any truncation classes or inline styles for `text-overflow: ellipsis` based on the container type. If we need to add a new modifier class or inline styles for container tabs, it would live here.

• packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.scss
  – This is the vanilla styles source for tabs (the SCSS that ultimately gets bundled into the CSS). It defines the rules for `.bx--tabs__nav-item` and its child `.bx--tabs__nav-link` in the default variant but (as reported) lacks the `overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; padding-right: 16px;` rules under the `.bx--tabs--container` modifier. We’ll need to add the missing selectors here so that container tabs truncate correctly.

• packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-test.js & packages/react/src/components/Tab/Tab-test.js
  – Once the code and/or CSS is updated, the existing snapshot/unit tests in these files will need to be updated or new tests added to verify that long labels get truncated in the container variant and that the `title` attribute is still set correctly for accessibility (showing the full label on hover).
2.bug_scenario: When you render the “container” style Tabs (by passing type="container"), any tab labels that are too long simply overflow—there is no text‐overflow or ellipsis applied on the tab links. In contrast, the “default” style Tabs correctly truncate long labels and show an ellipsis 16px from the edge, with the full label on the title attribute. The reproduced screenshots show that the container‐style tabs neither truncate nor ellipsize the text.
